## f3ecc20ad2d1

**Reproduced curriculum shortcut over the tested domain.** A rival that selects
the largest monochrome component, crops its bounding box, and recolors it cyan
fits all `3/3` unique canonical pairs and all `60/60` generated inputs evaluated
by the live canonical Racket rule (20 easy, 20 medium, 20 hard; seeds
9000–9059). The generated holed target is always a rectangular ring plus bumps
with at least eight cells, while distractors come from shapes of at most four
cells; the observed minimum largest-component margin was four. Thus these
samples never require detecting a hole, even though hole detection is the stated
concept.

Evidence: `checks/audit/f3ecc20ad2d1/largest_component_probe.json`, input batch
`checks/audit/f3ecc20ad2d1/input.json`, and Racket receipt
`checks/audit/f3ecc20ad2d1/racket.json`. The tested generator SHA-256 is
`d83ff78861ce6c7b2ff632141930d628c0d39752248c57353cb9b6f39c6221ea` and the
executed canonical rule hash is `84736dfacc09`. This is a finite, reproduced
shortcut on the listed canonical and generated samples, not a claim about every
possible lawful grid.

Lint and defect lint were also run without modifying the target; they report a
missing rule hash and dead/overlapping texture controls. A slower override run
was interrupted and is not counted as a completed result. No fix was made
because this was an audit-only target.
